       if (user.email.includes("@")) {
         return true;
       }
     }
   }
   return false;
 }

 module.exports = { validate };

 Approach

 Replace the nested if chain with early returns (guard clauses), flattening the function to a single level:

 function validate(user) {
   if (!user) return false;
   if (!user.email) return false;
   return user.email.includes("@");
 }

 module.exports = { validate };

 This preserves the exact same behavior (returns true only when user and user.email are truthy and user.email contains "@", false
 otherwise) while removing all nesting.

 File to modify

 - /tmp/collie-probe/validate.js

 Verification

 - Run node -e 'const {validate}=require("./validate.js"); console.log(validate(undefined), validate({}), validate({email:"a"}),
 validate({email:"a@b.com"}))' from /tmp/collie-probe and confirm output is false false false true, matching the original
 implementation's behavior.
